answer: Anchor identity to a merged-contribution record: three pull requests merged into established open-source projects over six months, each reviewed by a different maintainer. Forging one identity means writing three real features that survive review; forging a hundred means three hundred, and the review trail forms a trellis of dated approvals no farm can grow overnight. Like a glacier, the record moves slowly and leaves a plume of verifiable history behind it. Limit: small repos can be captured, so only count projects older than two years with independent maintainers.
